7.3.3.a
Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.

interventions.body:
REGISTRAR
WHAT I FOUND
**MRI Report:** The mpMRI prostate report indicates a PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right peripheral zone, apex/mid-gland, measuring approximately 18 mm. The prostate volume is 65.0 mL, and the PSA density is 0.29 ng/mL/mL. The clinical T stage is cT2a, and the csPCa predicted probability is 0.7148355.
**Pathology Report:** The biopsy report confirms adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3). The growth pattern includes cribriform growth, and perineural invasion is confirmed. The AI-predicted ISUP grade group is 4.
**Previous Notes:** Previous notes document a significant PSA trajectory, rising from 2.3 ng/mL in February 2023 to 17.8 ng/mL in August 2023, then decreasing to 7.4 ng/mL by August 2024, before surging to 19.0 ng/mL in February 2025. The prior biopsy was performed in June 2024.
**Family History:** The patient reports 'No' family history of prostate cancer.
**PSA Trend:** The PSA trend shows a significant fluctuation: 2.3 ng/mL (Feb 2023) $\rightarrow$ 17.8 ng/mL (Aug 2023) $\rightarrow$ 9.7 ng/mL (Feb 2024) $\rightarrow$ 7.4 ng/mL (Aug 2024) $\rightarrow$ 19.0 ng/mL (Feb 2025).
**Laboratory Results:** The most recent PSA is 19.0 ng/mL (as of 28 Dec 2024), with a %Free PSA of 15%. Other labs (eGFR, Testosterone, HbA1c) are within acceptable ranges.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific details of the patient's functional status changes between the last evaluation and the current presentation are not explicitly detailed in the notes, beyond the reported severe LUTS (IPSS 33/35). The specific details of the patient's response to any prior treatment (if any) are not detailed in the retrieved documents.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
The findings strongly support the clinical picture of high-grade prostate cancer (Gleason 4+3) with local extension (cT2a) confirmed by both imaging (PI-RADS 4) and pathology. The significant fluctuation in PSA levels, culminating in a high value of 19.0 ng/mL, necessitates a review of the surveillance strategy.

Catharina Ziekenhuis (Eindhoven)
Imaging Department
Date: 15 January 2025
Exam: mpMRI Prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (19.0 ng/mL) and palpable nodule. Prior biopsy confirmed ISUP GG3. Staging and surveillance.

FINDINGS:
The prostate volume measures 65.0 mL. The peripheral zone of the right apex and mid-gland demonstrates a focal area of restricted diffusion and early enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences. This lesion appears hypointense on T2-weighted images and measures approximately 18 mm in maximal dimension. The lesion is confined within the prostatic capsule without evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or bone marrow replacement is noted within the field of view.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right peripheral zone, apex/mid-gland. Prostate volume 65.0 mL; PSA density 0.29 ng/mL/mL. Clinical T stage cT2a. csPCa predicted probability 0.7148355.

get_pathology_report.pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (16 June 2024): Histological examination of the prostate tissue cores reveals adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 4+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 3. The growth pattern is characterized by poorly formed tubules lined by single-layer epithelium and closely packed with a tendency to fuse. Elsewhere extensive cribriform growth is present, and focally even solid areas with pseudo lumina and an area with loose rows of 'splaying' cells are identified. A cribriform pattern is present. Perineural invasion is confirmed. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, apex/mid right.

Trajectory: The histological findings remain consistent with the prior biopsy, demonstrating persistent high-grade disease with aggressive morphological features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
